gita:2:1: Arjuna slumped on the floor of his chariot between two waiting armies, eyes wet, his bow fallen at his feet, Krishna leaning close in blue and gold to begin speaking, grey dawn over Kurukshetra, a hushed and tender mood.
gita:2:2: Krishna standing upright in the chariot, one hand raised in challenge, his face firm and luminous, while behind the kneeling Arjuna a tall carved gateway dims as its lamps gutter out, ash-grey cloud, stern morning light.
gita:2:3: Krishna offering an open hand to lift Arjuna from his knees, the warrior's shoulders straightening as pale mist burns off the field, the first hard sunlight striking his armour, a mood of gathering resolve.
gita:2:4: Arjuna lowering his drawn arrow as he looks across the ranks at his white-bearded grandsire and his old teacher standing calm in the opposing line, morning haze between them, a mood of unbearable tenderness.
gita:2:5: A plain wooden begging bowl resting in the dust beside an abandoned golden throne and an untouched feast, one dark red stain spreading across the white cloth, low amber light in an empty pillared hall, a renouncing mood.
gita:2:6: A warrior standing between two identical bronze scale pans, each holding a crown and neither one tipping, his own kinsmen in armour facing him through the dust, flat overcast light, a mood of paralysing doubt.
gita:2:7: Arjuna kneeling with folded hands at Krishna's feet on the chariot floor, head bowed in surrender, Krishna's palm raised in blessing above him, warm gold breaking through cloud, a mood of humble asking.
gita:2:8: A grieving warrior turning his face away from heaped crowns and shining celestial palaces floating in the sky behind him, a small fire of sorrow reflected in his eyes, cold blue dusk, a mood of unconsolable loss.
gita:2:9: Arjuna seated in silence with his great bow laid across his knees, mouth closed and gaze fixed on nothing, Krishna waiting quietly at the reins, the two armies frozen and soundless, still grey light before sunrise.
gita:2:10: Krishna smiling gently at the reins between two vast armies, wholly unhurried, while Arjuna sits sunk in despair beside him, banners hanging in windless air, soft gold morning light on the chariot horses.
gita:2:11: Krishna speaking calmly with one hand lifted, while behind him the living and the departed stand together in the same quiet light as equal figures, a single unwavering flame between them, deep indigo sky, a serene mood.
gita:2:12: A chariot repeating endlessly into the horizon both behind and ahead, the same two figures riding in every one, a river with no visible source or mouth flowing beneath them all, timeless violet and gold light, a mood of unbroken being.
gita:2:13: One person shown three times in a single garden, a child, a young man and a white-haired elder, each carrying the same small steady flame at the heart, warm evening light through mango leaves, calm and unafraid.
gita:2:14: A seated ascetic unmoved on a stone terrace while monsoon rain lashes his left side and white desert sun blazes on his right, both weathers meeting over him, his face perfectly still, a mood of quiet endurance.
gita:2:15: A steady figure standing on a rock in the sea, a garland of marigolds falling on him from one side and a breaking wave striking the other, his stance identical to both, luminous dawn beyond the swell.
gita:2:16: A shimmering mirage city dissolving into empty desert air while a deep clear spring keeps welling from the rock beside it, two old seers watching without surprise, hard white noon light, a mood of clear discernment.
gita:2:17: A single thread of golden light passing through mountains, river, trees, animals and people alike, binding them all without disturbing any of them, an immense open sky at first light, a mood of quiet awe.
gita:2:18: Empty suits of armour lying like husks on the darkening field while a luminous figure rises unharmed above them and takes up a bow, Krishna's hand at his shoulder, red and gold storm light, a resolute mood.
gita:2:19: An arrow in flight passing straight through a tall standing flame that neither flickers nor breaks, the archer's face beyond it calm rather than triumphant, dark battlefield air, cool blue and ember light.
gita:2:20: An ancient oil lamp burning steadily inside a cracked clay vessel that is falling away in pieces around it, the flame untouched and unchanged, a dark shrine niche, deep blue shadow and old gold light.
gita:2:21: A warrior lowering his blade as he sees the same small light burning in the chest of the man opposite him, both faces softened by the recognition, dust hanging gold in low sun, a mood of disarmed clarity.
gita:2:22: A traveller folding away a threadbare sun-bleached robe on the steps of a river ghat and reaching for fresh saffron cloth laid ready, without ceremony or regret, morning light on wet stone, an unhurried mood.
gita:2:23: A single steady flame at the centre of four assaults, a sword edge, a sheet of fire, a rush of water and a driving wind, none of them touching or bending it, black storm sky pierced by gold, an invulnerable calm.
gita:2:24: An immense weathered stone pillar standing in the sea, unchanged while the seasons wheel around it, monsoon and drought and snow passing over in one frame, an ancient carved lotus at its base, vast still light.
gita:2:25: A curtained temple sanctum where only a warm glow escapes around the cloth and the form within is never shown, a devotee sitting content before it with grief set aside, deep blue night, drifting incense, a hushed mood.
gita:2:26: Waves rising and collapsing endlessly along a moonlit shore, each one a brief life, an old watcher seated above the tideline entirely at ease with the rhythm, silver and deep blue night, a tranquil mood.
gita:2:27: A great mango tree with ripe fruit dropping into the grass and young shoots pushing up from last season's fallen seed beneath it, both happening in the same warm afternoon light, a mood of accepted inevitability.
gita:2:28: Figures emerging from thick pale mist, walking briefly through a sunlit stretch of road where their faces are clear, then dissolving back into mist further on, soft dawn haze over fields, a gentle wondering mood.
gita:2:29: Three figures around a night fire, one gazing upward struck silent, one describing with an open hand, one leaning in to listen, and above them a sky none of them can quite hold, deep starlit blue, a mood of wonder.
gita:2:30: A quiet clearing at dusk where a man, a deer, a bird and an old ox each carry the same small steady light within them, no creature set above another, soft violet evening, a compassionate mood.
gita:2:31: A warrior straightening to full height and taking his bow from the chariot rail without hesitation, his own banner steady above him and every other path falling into shadow, hard clean morning light, a resolute mood.
gita:2:32: A carved stone doorway standing open in the middle of the battlefield, unasked for, warm light pouring through it onto a startled warrior who never went looking for it, dawn gold on dust, a mood of fortunate summons.
gita:2:33: A warrior walking away from an abandoned bow lying in the dust, his long shadow stretching behind him across the field and the light going out of the sky ahead, a cold hollow mood of duty set down.
gita:2:34: A once-honoured warrior walking through a village at dusk while people quietly turn their faces away, a garland trampled in the road behind him, dim smoky light, a heavy mood of lasting disgrace.
gita:2:35: Great chariot chiefs at the head of the army watching a comrade's chariot pull back from the line, their faces hardening from respect into judgement, dust rising between them, flat grey light, a bitter mood.
gita:2:36: Enemy warriors leaning on their chariots and laughing across the field at a rival's abandoned position, mouths open in mockery, his empty chariot small in the distance, hot glaring afternoon light, a stinging mood.
gita:2:37: A warrior rising to his feet in his chariot with shining celestial gates opening in the cloud above him and green fertile earth spreading below, both outcomes lit equally, sunrise breaking, a decisive mood.
gita:2:38: A calm warrior holding a perfectly level pair of scales at arm's length before stepping into battle, victory heaped in one pan and defeat in the other and weighing exactly the same, clear high morning light.
gita:2:39: Krishna raising two fingers as he turns from one teaching to the next, and at that moment heavy iron rings loosening and falling from a listener's wrists into the grass, warm gold light under a chariot canopy.
gita:2:40: A small clay lamp carried by a lone figure holding back an immense advancing darkness on a mountain road, the little flame steady and sufficient, none of its oil wasted, deep night blue against warm gold, a reassuring mood.
gita:2:41: One straight arrow flying true toward a single mark, and beside it a thicket of endlessly branching paths where a figure wanders in circles, clean morning light on the arrow and grey confusion in the thicket.
gita:2:42: Reciters in a flower-heaped pavilion chanting in delight at their own melody, blossoms drifting everywhere, while the shrine behind them stands unvisited and its lamp burns low, honeyed afternoon light, a seductive mood.
gita:2:43: An elaborate ritual fire ringed with offerings for wealth and pleasure, its smoke curling upward into a slowly turning wheel of cradles and funeral pyres, richly dressed patrons watching, orange firelight, a restless mood.
gita:2:44: A man trying to settle into meditation while fine golden cords tug at him from a palace, a treasury and a feast just beyond the doorway, his posture collapsing, lamps flickering, a mood of divided attention.
gita:2:45: A figure climbing above three coloured currents, white, red and smoke-grey, that braid across the valley below, reaching a bare still summit where the air is clear, high cold dawn light, a mood of liberation.
gita:2:46: A small carved stone water tank sitting beside a river in full flood, its carefully stored water suddenly beside the point, a brahmin standing knee-deep in the abundance and laughing, wide silver monsoon light.
gita:2:47: An archer at the instant of release, hand open and eyes calm, the arrow already gone beyond his control toward a target lost in mist, Krishna steady at the reins behind him, clean gold morning light, a focused mood.
gita:2:48: A figure crossing a stone causeway over still water with a shoulder-yoke held perfectly level, one basket marked by a garland and the other by ashes, neither dipping, an unbroken reflection below, calm even light.
gita:2:49: Two labourers at the same threshing floor, one hunched and anxious over the coins he expects, the other working freely beneath a hanging lamp of steady light, warm dusk over the fields, a quietly instructive mood.
gita:2:50: A master potter at the wheel shaping a vessel with effortless skill, wet clay ribboning away from his fingers and falling clean off his hands, a lamp beside him in the workshop, warm gold light, absorbed and unhurried.
gita:2:51: A caged bird set free and rising above a fruit orchard, the opened cage and the heavy ripe fruit left behind below, its flight already clear of the treetops toward pale gold sky, a mood of released ease.
gita:2:52: A traveller stepping out of a black clinging marsh onto clean sunlit stone, mud sliding from his legs, the water behind him settling clear enough to show the sky, the first bright light after rain, a relieved mood.
gita:2:53: A reader closing a palm-leaf manuscript and setting it aside, then sitting perfectly still with eyes shut on a temple veranda, the pages no longer pulling at him, quiet lamp glow, deep dusk blue, a mood of arrival.
gita:2:54: Arjuna turning to Krishna with an open questioning hand while three faint images of a serene sage appear beside them, one speaking, one seated, one walking a road, soft morning light, a mood of practical curiosity.
gita:2:55: A man setting a heavy bundle of glittering things down in the dust and sitting empty-handed against a warm stone wall, entirely content, nothing in his lap and nothing wanting, low honey-coloured evening light.
gita:2:56: A sage seated in a doorway as a hailstorm batters one end of the street and a festival procession blazes past the other, his face unchanged by either, torchlight and rain-glare mixing, a mood of settled steadiness.
gita:2:57: Two messengers arriving at once at a courtyard gate, one carrying a garland of victory and one a black cloth of loss, the seated householder receiving both with the same unhurried face, even grey afternoon light.
gita:2:58: A tortoise on a sunlit pond bank drawing its head and legs back under the shell, and beside it a sage folding his hands and closing his eyes in exactly the same gesture, still water, warm noon light, a composed mood.
gita:2:59: A fasting man seated before covered dishes he will not touch, the hunger still plain in his eyes, until a sunrise beyond the courtyard wall takes even the craving out of his face, cool blue turning to gold.
gita:2:60: Five wild horses dragging a chariot off the road despite the driver hauling back on the reins with all his strength, dust and scattered gear flying, hard afternoon light, a mood of alarming force.
gita:2:61: Five horses now gathered and standing quiet under a firm hand, the charioteer seated upright with his gaze fixed on Krishna ahead of him, the reins slack but sure, clear steady light, a mood of held control.
gita:2:62: A moth circling a lamp again and again, each pass closer, the small flame grown into a spitting fire in the next arch of the corridor, shadows leaping on the walls, deep night blue and angry orange, an ominous mood.
gita:2:63: A figure descending a broken stairway into rolling smoke, each step dimmer than the last, the lamps behind him going out one by one and the ground crumbling below, red glare fading to black, a mood of ruinous fall.
gita:2:64: A serene figure walking through a crowded bazaar of spices, silks and clamour, neither reaching for anything nor pulling away, the crowd parting easily around him, warm dappled market light, a mood of open calm.
gita:2:65: A lake settling into glass after a storm, the last ripples going out and the far mountains appearing whole in the reflection, an old woman at the ghat with her burdens set down, clear rinsed morning light.
gita:2:66: A man standing on a small raft that will not stop rocking in choppy water, unable to sit, unable to look at anything long enough to see it, joyless grey chop under a flat sky, a mood of exhausted restlessness.
gita:2:67: A small boat driven sideways across open water by a sudden squall, the oar useless in the boatman's hands and the shore he wanted sliding away behind him, dark green swell, torn silver light, a helpless drift.
gita:2:68: A boat drawn up and made fast in a sheltered cove while the wind spends itself outside the headland, five lamps burning steady in the rock niches above it, deep evening blue, a mood of secured stillness.
gita:2:69: A sage sitting awake and clear-eyed by a single lamp while an entire village sleeps around him under a vast starred sky, his eyes open on something the sleepers never see, deep indigo and silver, a solitary wakeful mood.
gita:2:70: Many rivers pouring into a great ocean from every side without raising it by a hand's breadth, the horizon perfectly level, gulls turning above the meeting waters, wide silver dawn light, an unmoved receptive mood.
gita:2:71: A wandering monk walking a dusty road at dawn with nothing in his hands, no bundle and no claim, his footprints the only mark he leaves, the fields on either side unowned and shining, soft pink and gold, a peaceful mood.
gita:2:72: An old man seated at the edge of the sea in the last hour of the day, delusion gone from his face, the small lamp beside him no longer distinguishable from the wide light it sits in, gold merging into violet, a serene mood.
gita:3:8: A household waking into its work at first light, a woman drawing water from the well, a man yoking oxen, smoke rising from the kitchen fire, the plain labour that keeps a body alive, warm apricot dawn, a willing mood.
gita:3:16: A great irrigation wheel turning between river and field, rain, harvest and offering feeding one another around it, while one man lounges apart taking only his own pleasure, gold afternoon light, a quietly accusing mood.
gita:3:19: A stonemason cutting steps into a hillside path day after day without pausing to admire them, his hands sure and unclenched, the hilltop shrine catching first light far above, cool blue morning, a mood of steady ascent.
gita:3:21: A respected elder stopping to bow at a wayside shrine, and behind him, unasked, a line of villagers and children doing the same, the gesture spreading down the road, warm low sun, a mood of quiet influence.
gita:3:27: Wind bending a whole forest, a river turning a mill and fire cooking grain, all of it happening by itself, while a small figure stands in the middle with his chest out claiming the work as his, ironic gold light.
gita:3:30: A warrior laying his weapons at Krishna's feet, then lifting them again with the fever gone out of his face, no hope and no self-display left in the gesture, cool clear light before battle, a surrendered readiness.
gita:3:35: A farmer steady behind his own plough in a modest field while a merchant's glittering caravan passes on the high road, his furrow straight and unenvious, dust gold in the late sun, a mood of contented belonging.
gita:3:37: A vast open-mouthed fire in the shape of a devouring shadow rising at a city gate, everything thrown into it vanishing without filling it, a lone armed figure facing it squarely, black smoke and red glare, a named danger.
gita:3:42: A tiered temple rising in clear steps, each level brighter than the one below, the body at its base and the senses, mind and reason above it, a single unwavering light in the topmost shrine, dawn gold, an ordered ascent.
gita:3:43: A steadied warrior raising a blade of pure light against a many-headed shape of craving that keeps regrowing, his own face calm and his footing sure, deep blue dusk shot with gold, a mood of hard but certain combat.
gita:4:7: Righteousness thinning like a field going brown and lamps guttering along a temple wall, while high above the cloud gathers into a luminous blue form beginning to take shape, storm light broken by gold, an imminent mood.
gita:4:8: Krishna standing with a sheltering arm over the frightened and the just, a discus of light turning at his shoulder, a fallen tyrant's crown in the dust, a temple being raised again behind them, sunrise gold, a restoring mood.
gita:4:11: Many different pilgrim roads, a forest track, a desert trail, a river ghat and a mountain stair, all bending toward the same hilltop shrine, each traveller met by the same light, wide evening gold, a generous welcoming mood.
gita:4:18: A great cartwheel spinning at speed while its hub stays perfectly still, and beside it a seated sage whose stillness is doing a quiet work of its own, gold dust hanging in the light, a mood of paradox held calmly.
gita:4:20: A weaver working his loom all day with no thought of the price of the cloth, his shuttle flying and his face untroubled, the finished lengths piling behind him unclaimed, warm slanting light through a doorway, an easy mood.
gita:4:24: A fire offering in which the ladle, the poured ghee, the flame and the hands of the priest are all made of the same golden substance, the shrine dissolving into that one light, deep amber glow, a mood of unified vision.
gita:4:34: A student lying full-length in respect before a forest teacher's seat, then rising to carry firewood and water for him unasked, the old man's eyes kind, dappled green light under tall trees, a mood of earned learning.
gita:4:38: Raw ore refined in a goldsmith's fire until the pure metal runs clear, and beside the workshop a jar of muddy water standing untouched until it settles bright, patient afternoon light, a mood of slow purification.
gita:4:39: A young seeker kneeling with steady faith before a lit shrine lamp, senses gathered and hands folded, the peace arriving in his face at once like sunrise reaching a courtyard, warm gold on white stone, a serene mood.
gita:4:42: A luminous blade cutting through a thick knotted cord coiled at a warrior's heart, the severed ends falling away and the man rising to his feet with his bow in hand, first sun striking the field, a decisive clearing.
gita:6:5: A climber hauling himself up onto a high ledge by his own hand and no one else's, while his own shadow below seems to pull the other way, a hermitage lamp on the summit above, cold dawn light, a mood of self-reliance.
gita:6:6: A man kneeling at a still pool where his reflection meets him as a steady companion, while in the broken water further along the same face glares back like an enemy, twilight blue and gold, an inward reckoning.
gita:6:16: A narrow lit path running between two dark extremes, a groaning banquet spilling over on one side and a bare starving cell on the other, a yogi walking calmly down the middle, balanced evening light, a measured mood.
gita:6:17: A whole day laid out in one courtyard, a modest meal on a leaf plate, a walking path, a set of tools at rest and a plain sleeping mat, everything in due proportion, calm even daylight, a mood of unhurried order.
gita:6:19: A single lamp burning in a windless inner room, its flame absolutely upright and unwavering, the still air around it almost visible, a meditating figure just beyond in soft shadow, deep warm gold, a gathered stillness.
gita:6:26: A cowherd walking out again and again to bring a straying calf back to the herd, unhurried and without anger, the same patient path worn across the meadow, soft green and gold afternoon, a mood of gentle persistence.
gita:6:30: A seeker standing in a river valley where the same blue-gold presence shows through the water, the trees, the cattle and the passing people, and equally in his own chest, luminous morning haze, an unbroken connection.
gita:6:35: A wild horse gentled over long days by a patient hand and a simple rope, its head lowering at last, the worn track of that work circling the paddock, warm dusty gold light, a mood of hard-won steadiness.
gita:6:40: A young sapling planted by a traveller years before, now grown and sheltering the road for others, the man himself walking on unharmed under a wide clear sky, warm late gold, a mood of assured safety.
gita:6:47: Many practitioners on one hillside, some in postures, some in study, some tending a fire, and one seated apart with his whole heart simply turned toward Krishna in the dawn, gold light singling him out, a tender mood.
gita:7:3: A vast crowd filling a plain, a thin line of climbers on the mountain path above them, and a single figure standing in the light at the summit, the scale honest and sobering, cool blue distance and gold peak, a searching mood.
gita:7:7: Worlds, suns and small bright lives strung like gems along a fine golden thread that runs through everything and is barely visible, Krishna's hand holding one end in the dark, deep cosmic blue, a mood of hidden unity.
gita:7:14: A wide river of shifting three-coloured mist that swallows swimmers who try to force it, while a small boat carries those who have taken refuge safely toward a lit far shore, moonlit blue, a mood of guided crossing.
gita:7:16: Four figures approaching one shrine at dusk, a weeping man in trouble, a student with a question, a merchant asking for gain, and a serene sage who wants nothing, all received by the same lamp, warm gold, a welcoming mood.
gita:7:19: An old pilgrim arriving at the last shrine after a road that has crossed many lifetimes, worn milestones disappearing into mist behind him, recognition breaking over his face, deep gold evening, a rare and quiet mood.
gita:9:22: A traveller walking with his eyes on one distant light while unseen hands set water and bread on the path ahead of him and keep watch over what he left behind, soft protective moonlight, a mood of quiet provision.
gita:9:26: A poor devotee laying a single green leaf, one flower, a small fruit and a cup of water on a village altar with both hands, the shrine lamp brightening as if pleased, humble evening gold, a mood of accepted simplicity.
gita:9:27: A day of ordinary acts turned into offering, a meal lifted briefly before eating, coins pressed into a beggar's hand, tools set down at a household shrine, each gesture inclined toward the lamp, warm gold, a devout mood.
gita:9:29: Krishna standing in even light that falls identically on rich and poor, saint and outcast, animal and bird, while those who turn their faces toward him glow with that same light from within, wide serene dawn, a tender mood.
gita:9:30: A man with a hard scarred face kneeling for the first time at a roadside shrine, his weapons set down in the dust behind him, the lamp remaking his features into something new, deep dusk blue and warm flame, a turning mood.
gita:9:34: A devotee at full prostration before Krishna with mind, hands and whole body given at once, a single path of light running from his heart to the deity, a night-blue sanctum, doubled lamp flames, a mood of complete surrender.
gita:12:1: Arjuna standing with a question between two ways of worship, on one side Krishna's warm familiar form and on the other a vast unshaped brightness with no outline at all, dawn between them, a mood of honest inquiry.
gita:12:2: Devotees seated in unbroken rows facing Krishna at first light, every gaze steady and unwandering, faith plain in their faces, the lamps in their hands all leaning the same way, clear gold morning, a unified attentive mood.
gita:12:3: An empty stone sanctum holding no image at all, only immeasurable light filling the space, an ascetic seated before that absence entirely at peace, cold pure white and blue, a mood of formless reverence.
gita:12:4: A yogi with senses gathered kneeling to tend an injured animal at a village well, treating the beggar and the merchant beside him at the same level, the same even care in every direction, calm midmorning light.
gita:12:5: A climber on a sheer blank cliff of pale stone with no handhold and no image to hold on to, wind pulling at his cloth, an easier lamplit stair visible far to one side, high thin light, a mood of arduous effort.
gita:12:6: A worker setting the day's finished labour down at Krishna's feet like a harvest, then sitting before him with nothing else in view, his tools resting to one side, warm lamp-lit evening, a mood of undivided offering.
gita:12:7: A hand of blue light reaching down into a heaving dark ocean to lift a drowning figure clear of the water, other swimmers turning toward it, the storm breaking into gold at the horizon, a mood of swift rescue.
gita:12:8: A devotee seated inside a luminous blue form as if within a lit house, mind and reason both at rest there, the world small beyond the doorway, deep indigo and warm gold, a mood of settled dwelling.
gita:12:9: A pupil returning to the same seat at the same hour again and again, the mat worn thin beneath him, a teacher watching without impatience from the doorway, grey early light, a mood of forgiving repetition.
gita:12:10: A woman sweeping a temple courtyard and a man carrying water up its steps, ordinary work done wholly for the deity's sake, the shrine lamp bright ahead of them, warm morning gold on wet stone, a mood of humble service.
gita:12:11: A farmer leaving the first and best of his harvest at a shrine and walking away without counting it, his hands steady and his face untroubled, the loaded cart going on down the road, soft dusk, a quiet relinquishment.
gita:12:12: Four rising steps carved into a hillside, practice, knowledge, meditation and open-handed release, the topmost one bare and lit, a figure who has just let something fall from his hand standing in sudden calm, gold dawn.
gita:12:13: A traveller sharing his food with a stray dog and a hostile stranger alike at a roadside fire, no grudge anywhere in his face, his small bundle unguarded beside him, warm firelight against blue night, a forgiving mood.
gita:12:14: A householder seated in contentment on a plain veranda whether the harvest was good or thin, his practice unbroken and his mind given over, a lamp and a folded shawl beside him, soft amber dusk, a steady devoted mood.
gita:12:15: A man passing quietly through a noisy street festival, disturbing nobody and disturbed by nothing, drums and crowds flowing around him untouched, elation and anger both absent from his face, warm torchlight, a serene mood.
gita:12:16: A skilled carpenter finishing a shrine door with clean sure hands and no plans for what it will bring him, his workshop swept bare and nothing waiting to be launched, clear north light through the window, an unburdened mood.
gita:12:17: A ferryman rowing steadily as a wedding party waits on one bank and a funeral party on the other, giving each the same passage, neither gladdened nor darkened, wide grey-gold river light, an even-handed calm.
gita:12:18: A mendicant standing unchanged as one crowd garlands him and another jeers, snow blowing on his right and hot sun on his left, his expression identical in every quarter, cold blue meeting warm gold, an unshakeable mood.
gita:12:19: A silent wandering monk asleep under a tree with no roof of his own, content with whatever the day gave him, praise and blame from the village behind him equally faded, moonlight through leaves, a homeless peaceful mood.
gita:12:20: Devotees walking a lamp-lit road together behind a teaching that does not age, each carrying a small flame lit from one source, Krishna radiant at the road's end, deep blue night and gold, a mood of cherished belonging.
gita:15:1: An immense peepul tree hanging upside down from the sky, its roots spreading into the light above and its branches reaching down into the world, its leaves shining like sung hymns, deep cosmic blue and gold, an awestruck mood.
gita:15:5: A pilgrim reaching a high pass with pride and delusion shed like heavy garments left on the rocks behind him, the pull of craving turned away, steady beyond heat and cold, clear thin dawn light, a mood of eternal arrival.
gita:15:7: A small flame of the same substance as a great cosmic light descending into a human form, gathering five slender rays of the senses and the mind about itself like a garment, deep blue into warm gold, a tender embodiment.
gita:15:15: Krishna seated in a small radiant shrine within the heart of every figure in a village scene, the same lamp inside farmer, child, elder and ox, memory and knowing flowing out from it, warm gold on indigo, an intimate mood.
gita:18:14: Five parts of one act shown together, the body, the doer, the ranked senses, the many separate efforts, and above them a faint presiding deity belonging to none of them, ordered gold and blue light, a contemplative mood.
gita:18:23: A priest performing an ordained rite with clean unhurried hands, no eagerness and no distaste in his face, the offering complete and nothing expected back, plain white cloth and clear morning light, a mood of pure execution.
gita:18:47: A village blacksmith working his own small forge while a grander armoury glitters across the lane, the plain blade in his tongs honest and his own, sparks rising in the dark, warm red and gold firelight, a rightful mood.
gita:18:48: A cooking fire burning well with grey smoke inevitably curling off it, a woman tending it without complaint at dawn, no fire in the village without its smoke, soft blue haze and orange flame, an accepting mood.
gita:18:56: A boatman working his oars steadily across a wide river while a following wind of grace fills the sail behind him, his labour and the carrying both plain in one frame, gold light on the current, a mood of assisted effort.
gita:18:58: A narrow mountain pass where fallen boulders open before a traveller whose eyes are on the shrine light ahead, while another figure, deaf with pride, strides into the rockfall behind him, hard shadow and gold, a cautionary mood.
gita:18:61: Countless small figures riding the rim of an immense turning wheel of the world, each one moved by a light seated at its still centre, gears of season and fate below, deep cosmic blue and gold, a mood of vast mechanism.
gita:18:63: Krishna sitting back with an open palm after the last teaching, giving the choice entirely away, Arjuna in thought with his bow across his knees, the chariot quiet between two armies, level golden light, a granted freedom.
gita:18:66: A man laying an armload of heavy obligations down at Krishna's feet like bundled firewood and stepping forward empty-handed into an embrace of blue-gold light, grief lifting from his face, radiant dawn, a total refuge.
gita:18:78: Krishna at the reins and Arjuna with his bow standing together in one chariot at sunrise, the field steady around them, prosperity and victory implied in their easy alignment, banners lifting, wide gold light, a confident mood.
